We suggest combining word and phrase representations with context information and contextual dependencies extracted from semantic fields to enhance the accuracy of text classification. By utilizing this hybrid model in conjunction with a support vector machine for predicting movie genres, our approach outperforms existing methods such as CBOW and Skip-Gradients in the Kaggle Movie Genre Identification challenge.

As the number of nodes in a random geometric graph grows, we examine the structure of the largest node subgroup within the graph. This analysis focuses on the maximum number of nodes that can be separated without any two being directly connected, along with the diameter of the largest such subgroup within the graph. To determine these values, we consider a plane with nodes being randomly located at points that adhere to a specific density threshold, and two distance-based connection criteria: one based on the Euclidean distance and the other on the Manhattan distance. Our research findings reveal that when the number of nodes grows without bound, the maximum number of disconnected subgroups within the graph is finite and the same for both connection criteria. Conversely, the largest diameter within the graph is found to be significantly distinct across these two distance metrics.

A novel method for constructing rotating stars in relativity is introduced, based on applying the Euler-Heintze pressure tensor, which enables the conversion of solutions to the Euler equations into equivalent solutions to the Bianchi equations describing spacetime geometry. This allows for the generation of rotating relativistic star models within the nonlinear sigma-model framework, offering a Lagrangian-based construction distinct from the standard Einstein method.

A novel, anisotropic, spherically symmetric metric has been formulated using the Generalized Lema\^{\i}tre-Tolman-Bondi model in conjunction with Palatini $f(R)$ gravity. This approach yields a four-dimensional action that naturally leads to a non-minimally coupled scalar field. Consequently, the scalar field decouples from matter, while the gravitational field is coupled. In the presence of this coupling, the field equations yield a non-standard solution, which deviates from the standard GLEMA-Tolman-Bondi metric. Notably, the standard Lema\^{\i}te-Tolman-Bondi metric is recovered when the non-minimal coupling is set to zero.

In an N-partite quantum system, if entanglement confirmation is possible for all participants using only local tests, these measurements are described as product measurements. Conversely, if no set of product measurements can consistently confirm entanglement, these systems are termed 'generalized separable'. A key theorem in quantum nonlocality, initially proposed for three qubits, states separability is impossible. Our research generalizes this principle to separable states across any N-dimensional Hilbert space, demonstrating that entanglement confirmation is impossible for all finite N-partite settings, as product measurements are insufficient. Furthermore, this finding has significant implications for separable state detection and the nonlocality of quantum correlations.

Recent studies have shown that deep learning models can accurately predict Web User Visual Attention (WUVA) patterns. Visual attention is crucial for user interaction and can be used to pre-render content, including text, images, and videos. Current WUVA models rely on either simulating user behavior or using real user gaze data. However, user behavior models lack accuracy, while gaze data is limited to specific user sessions. To overcome these limitations, we present a deep learning model that continuously estimates WUVA for Web pages. Our model uses a recurrent deep convolutional neural network to predict attention distribution based on user behavior, session ID, and page history. We also propose a novel metric, Mean Absolute Error with Weighted Sum (MAEWS), to measure the model's performance. Using a large dataset from 150,000 users, we show that our model achieves MAEWS of 0.039, outperforming other models. Furthermore, we demonstrate the model's ability to accurately predict WUVA for short-term periods ranging from 1-10 seconds based on limited input data.

A reconfigurable intelligent surface is a cutting-edge technology being researched for use in the next generation of wireless communication systems. This study presents, develops, and experimentally evaluates a novel design for a transparent RIS capable of modifying the path lengths of incoming electromagnetic signals. The RIS consists of highly flexible, carbon-based nanotube composite materials that are arranged in a two-dimensional grid and controlled by an external voltage. An algorithmic approach is proposed to adjust the phase angles of the RIS unit cells, ensuring optimal performance. This design is then tested in various applications, including signal phase adjustment and enhanced performance in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Experimental results are provided to demonstrate the RIS's ability to manage electromagnetic waves in the visible light spectrum.

Offline reinforcement learning, particularly with the use of function approximation, has garnered significant attention. Various approaches have been proposed, but they are heavily dependent on specific assumptions regarding the model, which not all problems can satisfy. Consequently, there has been a renewed focus on frameworks supporting multiple problem formulations and providing more general conditions for convergence. A notable framework was proposed by Chen et al., which involved a linear programming structure, and demonstrated a guaranteed lower bound on the performance of any offline RL algorithm under this framework. This study revisits this framework, focusing on the case where the operator and context transformation functions are representable by any pre-specified set of functions. A novel algorithm is presented that achieves the lower bound and, when optimized, converges at a rate comparable to that of online gradient descent with a fixed step size.

We derive a generalization of a key idea in Path Original's algorithm, originally designed to identify identical paths in directed and undirected graphs, through a process of functional modification and subsequent adaptation. By reversing the steps of the initial reduction, we can construct reverse homotopies from standard to reverse homotopies, and vice versa, yielding a versatile framework for representing and manipulating graph homotopies. A diverse set of examples demonstrates the utility of this framework, enabling users to implement their own custom graph homotopy functions.

A recently discovered galaxy, J0437+2456, is an unusual type known as a broad-line radio galaxy. A close examination of the galaxy's central area has revealed the presence of two distinct radio sources, J043700+2456.3 and J043700+2456.8. Research suggests that these sources are connected by a bridge of radio emissions and are moving at a combined rate of 0.37 arcseconds per year, with the latter source possibly representing a newly formed black hole. A calculated estimate of the time it took for the newly formed black hole to emerge, approximately 2.3 million years, is consistent with the expected timeframe for the feeding and activation of a supermassive black hole. A close comparison of the galaxy's radio emissions indicates that the primary and secondary sources emit radio emissions at significantly different frequencies, with the secondary source possibly experiencing a more rapid increase in emissions. A calculated estimate of the galaxy's accretion rate is also provided, showing that the newly formed black hole in J043700+2456.8 is likely consuming its surrounding material at a faster rate than the existing black hole. A close examination of the galaxy's radio emissions reveals that the primary and secondary sources emit radio emissions in different directions, with the primary source emitting a more symmetrical shape than the secondary source.

This paper examines ten configurations in the planar Newtonian three-body problem where a small, third body moves close to two massive, spatially extended objects. It shows that eight of these configurations result in the outer body's distance from the other two varying continuously, while the other two configurations create singularities in this parameter. Additionally, specific conditions are determined under the $-1/3 < \mu < 1$ constraint where two massive objects are Earth and the Moon, and the third body is a spacecraft or lunar module.

FLIM is an imaging technique that measures the temporal dynamics of fluorescent molecules. By analyzing the decay curves, it's possible to gain information about the environment's influence on fluorescence lifetime at a molecular level. However, experimental constraints often necessitate approximating the decay with a limited number of exponential components. When accurate multi-exponential decays are sought, deconvolution becomes a crucial step in the processing pipeline. This paper explores the deconvolution process, its underlying principles, and associated trade-offs.

This research introduces a Graph Convolution-based framework to enhance the effectiveness of personalized product search by analyzing users' past behaviors and current interests. Personalized product search is a critical e-commerce function that tailors product suggestions to individual users' preferences. Existing methods often rely on content analysis or collaborative filtering, but they can be limited by the information they have access to. In contrast, this proposed framework leverages both product and user content, as well as interactions between them. Specifically, it uses two separate graphs to represent a user's potential interests and the relationships between products, and applies a Graph Convolutional Network to learn dynamic features based on a user's historical behaviors. These dynamic features are then combined with the user's current interests to improve personalized product search results. Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework.

In recent years, techniques for analyzing graph data have gained significant attention. One widely used approach is graph embedding, which aims to represent graphs in a condensed space while preserving their inherent structure and properties. Typically, this representation is achieved by mapping nodes to vectors, but a new challenge has arisen with the need to represent nodes based on their attributes. When node attributes are not available, researchers have turned to semi-supervised and unsupervised methods, but these come with their own limitations. To overcome these issues, this study introduces a novel framework for deep manifold-attributed graph embedding, which is fully unsupervised and can incorporate node attributes. By preserving the geometric structure of graphs and attributing nodes, this model can be effectively used for classification tasks, outperforming existing methods and showcasing its adaptability across various real-world datasets.

In massive machine-type communications (mMTC), granting numerous users low-latency connections is a significant challenge due to the need for a grant-free approach. This can be achieved by using non-orthogonal power-domain multiple access (NOMA) at base stations, facilitated by pre-coded grant-free massive connectivity sequences. However, granting multiple users requires designing these sequences to minimize interference among them, thereby maximizing the number of granted users. This paper presents a two-stage genetic algorithm for designing these sequences, involving an initial stage that uses a multi-objective genetic algorithm to find a Pareto-frontier of feasible sequences, and a second stage that uses a ranking-based genetic algorithm to refine the search space. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the traditional genetic algorithm, enabling a higher number of granted users.

Compressed sensing explores algorithms to retrieve a sparse signal or code from lower-dimensional data, typically relying on access to the transformation matrix. However, this approach is limited when the matrix is unknown, such as in encrypted communication. To address this "blind compressive sensing" challenge, we develop a new algorithm that uses the encoding matrix as the primary focus, rather than the original signal. This enables us to identify the encoding matrix parameters through iterative refinement, ultimately allowing us to decrypt the original signal. Our proposed algorithm is flexible, adaptable to different conditions in the transformation matrix, and effectively applicable to both real and complex sparse signals.

Domain shift poses a significant challenge in supervised learning, where policy updates are hindered by this problem. This issue arises from differences between source data and reward distributions, as well as distribution shifts that occur outside the scope of the model. Our research focuses on a learning from demonstrations setting, where a source policy is available and nearly optimal. We investigate whether leveraging transformations of the state and reward reward samples from the target distribution can mitigate the negative effects of domain shift on policy performance. Our approach involves using adversarial learning to learn these transformations. We demonstrate that this method can learn a robust value function that remains unaffected by domain shift and achieves higher sample-based policy performance than models without transformations. Our research also reveals that the target transformations have desirable properties, including invariance and a data compression effect that contributes to improved generalization and robustness. We also explore a novel framework called Random Transformation Selection (RTS), which selects a single transformation at each adaptation step. Our results show that RTS achieves comparable performance to adversarial learning models and is more efficient, while offering greater robustness to model capacity and thus is a more reliable choice in practice.

This paper aims to classify and analyze derivations under two specific conditions. Firstly, we investigate and characterize 2-local derivations in the context of Lie type algebras defined within Jordan matrix ring (JMR) structures formed by commutative, inversive rings. Additionally, we define and classify local derivations under the same conditions, resulting in a discovery that reveals 2-local derivations to be equivalent to local derivations. Consequently, we identify that every derivation on the JMR structure corresponds to both a 2-local and a local derivation. Secondly, we investigate and characterize derivations within the broader framework of Jordan matrix ring (JMR) structures formed by commutative, inversive rings, resulting in a discovery that local derivations on JMR structures exhibit distinct properties and do not necessarily adhere to the previously established characterization.

Berry's phase is explored through the lens of Dirac monopole in a magnetic field that is constantly changing in time. The system is then stabilized using the Lagrangian formalism, which results in a new constant magnetic field that no longer experiences Dirac monopole. The system is then analyzed in the context of the quantum state's adiabatic evolution with respect to the changed magnetic field, which leads to an understanding of the Berry phase. The study also examines how the phase factor is influenced by the angle at which a closed path is oriented in the momentum space.

This work explores compacton formation in a Bose-Einstein condensate with interaction enabled, taking into account both spin-orbit coupling and density-dependent interaction scenarios. Employing a variational approach, we find that spin-orbit coupling has a negligible effect when weakly present, but significantly hampers or prevents compacton formation when sufficiently strong. Notably, in the density-dependent interaction case, spin-orbit coupling actually promotes compacton formation. Additionally, we have derived the first integrals of the mean-field nonlinear Schrodinger equation and analyzed the relationship between compacton properties, such as amplitude and frequency, to the strength of spin-orbit coupling. Furthermore, we have investigated the connection between the energy spectrum of compactons and the wave number in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.

The heavy-quark spin symmetry effects in the $P$-wave charmed baryon decays are explored using the unquenched lattice QCD. The study involves using two types of lattice actions, improved staggered and clover quarks. The resulting masses for $P$-wave charmed baryons are around 2595 and 2625 MeV. The analysis of the strong couplings between $P$-wave and $S$-wave charmed baryons reveals that the partial decay width for the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ to $\eta_\mathbb{B} p$ is 21.2 keV, while the partial width for the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ to $\eta_\mathbb{B} p$ is 49.5 keV. The study suggests that the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ is likely not the heavy-quark spin symmetry partner of the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, as it exhibits weaker coupling with $\eta_\mathbb{B} p$.

This paper explores a specific type of non-Euclidean space, known as a Lie group broken by a subgroup, and investigates the ability to accurately approximate continuous functions on the resulting orbit space using smooth functions. The key findings demonstrate that under certain conditions, including Gelfand pairs and Riemannian symmetric spaces, a sequence of smooth functions exists that approximates the continuous functions on the orbit space in the uniform topology of families on compact subsets.

We examine the potential of discovering axion-like particles (ALPs) and the utility of their properties in our proposal for a new muon collider. This facility will enable us to investigate a broad range of parameters, including the mass, mixing ratio, and coupling constants of ALPs through the examination of muon decay patterns. By utilizing a combination of experimental approaches, such as the observation of missing energy and events with a single positron, we aim to explore the parameter space of ALPs. This will involve a multi-faceted experimental strategy involving various collision energies, aiming to achieve the following key goals: a comprehensive exploration of ALP parameters, particularly in terms of mixing ratio and axion-photon coupling, and the identification of ALP masses that are particularly amenable to study.

This research introduces the Open-Src-MetaSys framework, an open-source, fully functional system for metadata management in future in-memory databases. It features a dynamic, process-aware interface that enables flexible interface selection and efficient interface interface transition. Moreover, the framework incorporates energy-efficient techniques such as interface idleness detection, dynamic interface reduction, and adaptive interface overlap. We present both the proposed metadata management system and its optimization methods, along with experimental results on a range of workloads across 16-bit and 32/64-bit systems.

The recent surge in transfer learning's popularity is attributed to the efficiency and high performance it offers in various applications. This work focuses on developing transfer learning schemes for medical image analysis, which faces challenges due to limited availability of annotated data. We introduce two novel approaches for tackling this issue: leveraging Siamese networks to utilize unlabeled pairs of images, and generating synthetic data through semantic image manipulation. Two distinct transfer learning frameworks are presented, which can be adapted according to the selected siamese architecture and the type of generated data. We evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed schemes on benchmark medical datasets, which show promising results when compared to traditional data augmentation methods.

A collection of elliptic equations, each with quasilinear, convective terms and nonlinear coefficients, is analyzed over a given domain in $N$-dimensional space. In this study, we examine the existence of solutions, focusing on regularity and its loss, and investigate multiple solutions within specific parameter ranges. To prove existence, we combine a fixed-point method with an initial energy estimate, and also develop a local and global regularity result. Furthermore, we investigate the existence of solutions for a related problem with an unusual feature: a relationship between the nonlinear coefficients and their derivatives that leads to a unique challenge.

Recurrent Neural Networks, crucial for sequence modeling and time series forecasting, are hindered in their ability to retain and update long-term information by the vanishing gradient issue. Existing solutions often come at the cost of increased model complexity, but we propose an alternative approach in the form of a Fourier Recurrent Unit, a cutting-edge model capable of learning long-term dependencies efficiently and minimizing gradient explosion. By utilizing a Fourier series-based model architecture, our proposed unit outperforms its existing counterparts and rivals state-of-the-art solutions. We achieve this by leveraging the Fourier series' inherent periodic characteristics to update hidden unit states, thereby facilitating gradient propagation through the network. Our proposed architecture is scalable, allowing for the use of a wide range of basis functions such as Fourier and wavelet series, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing recurrent networks as a drop-in replacement. Experimental results confirm that the proposed unit effectively models long-term dependencies and surpasses its performance metrics.

In Markov Decision Processes, an agent aims to reach a desired state from a given starting state by making sequential decisions. The key issue is whether we can create a low-regret policy, where the agent's expected long-term regret when taking the optimal actions is minimized. While the problem has been solved for certain scenarios, it remains unsolved for general Markov Decision Processes. This study develops a theoretical framework to tackle this issue, which yields optimal solutions for specific cases. Furthermore, a novel algorithm is created for general Markov settings analogous to a known technique in Markov perfect bands. The algorithm's performance is evaluated in a new setting where transitions are unknown, and it is proven to be competitive.

A groundbreaking technique has been developed to produce extremely intense, linearly polarized X-ray electron beams by utilizing dual electron laser pulses. This innovative method, referred to as dual-wake injection, is capable of producing attosecond electron pulses, and its potential for applications in next-generation particle accelerators and X-ray imaging is substantial. The concept of dual-wake injection has shown that it can achieve linear polarization, and research has found that polarization symmetry is contingent upon the ratio of laser pulse duration to electron bunch duration. The duration of electron pulses, and subsequently their X-ray pulses, can be determined by adjusting the ratio of laser pulse duration to electron bunch duration. This innovative method, and subsequent technique, can be applied to any electron storage ring to produce X-ray pulses as short as attoseconds by utilizing laser pulse duration and electron bunch duration ratio as variables. The development of such a compact X-ray source is crucial for advancing next-generation particle accelerators and X-ray imaging technologies.

The universe's most intricate and elaborate structures are found in living organisms. The notion that life can arise from chance, supported by the theory of natural selection, is a conflicting perspective with the possibility that life is an inherent part of the universe. An alternative explanation for the emergence of life is that it adheres to fundamental physical principles, such as the laws of conservation of energy and matter, and adheres to specific physical laws. This idea is based on a model that suggests life originates from systems that exhibit simplicity and clarity, and through a process of gradual evolution, these systems become more intricate and disordered. This model, grounded in the principles of thermodynamics, aims to bridge the gap between inanimate matter and living organisms. This article presents an astrophysical perspective on the origin of life, focusing on the role of energy and matter transport within celestial environments. The presence of magnetic flux tubes, which facilitate the transport of energy and matter, is a common feature across various astrophysical settings. These tubes enable the transmission of energy and matter, and play a crucial part in the formation of intricate and disordered systems. The presence of simplicity and clarity is a characteristic of the systems within the tubes, and they serve as a conduit for the emergence of complexity and disorder. The systems within the tubes are shielded from external sources of disorder by the tubes, and they are protected from the effects of radiation. The paper explores the concept of 'climate change research' and defines its scope within the context of scientific, technical, and statistical studies. It discusses how an increasing volume of such research is published within an open-access framework, making it accessible to a broader audience, including policymakers, in a data set. To this end, the paper combines Web Of Scopus and OpenDOAR data, along with a Named Entity Recognition tool, to create a comprehensive repository of research publications and funding, which is then quantified and analyzed. Furthermore, the paper illustrates the potential of using this data in developing predictive models to identify relevant factors linked to the impact of climate change research, thereby providing insights for policymakers to shape an evidence-based R&D policy.

The most commonly utilized smartphone operating systems, Android and Linux, are susceptible to side-channel leaks due to their kernel-level security vulnerabilities. The Linux kernel's recent introduction of the Logarithmic Security Feature Checker (LSFChk) in 2020 has helped mitigate the problem to some extent, but its effectiveness is limited as it only addresses a specific category of log-based side-channels. To address this issue more effectively, this research proposes a solution to detect side-channel leaks in systems with no log-based leaks. The developed tool, ASVAAN, efficiently semi-automatically identifies side-channel leaks in Android NDK programs by utilizing a combination of pattern matching and symbolic execution techniques. The tool's capabilities were successfully demonstrated through a series of experiments, including the detection of side-channel leaks in three real-world programs and the accurate recovery of leaked variables for up to 99% of the leaks detected.

Ethereum has emerged as the leading platform for building and deploying decentralized applications, necessitating a deeper understanding of user behavior and transaction patterns. A study of user transaction networks, labeled by exchange, lending, and DeFi platforms, reveals distinct characteristics and ego network properties. A comparison of ego network characteristics and transaction labels reveals that individuals involved in DeFi activities exhibit the greatest variation in transaction patterns. Furthermore, temporal analysis of ego network properties and transaction labels reveals that individuals involved in DeFi activities exhibit the greatest consistency in transaction patterns over time.

Researchers have observed a unique quantum response in a specially prepared two-dimensional electron system at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface. By adjusting the level of illumination, they were able to adjust the concentration of electrons in the system and induce a quantum oscillation pattern. These patterns consisted of a combination of frequencies that shifted as the concentration of electrons changed, and the system demonstrated a specific level of effective mass. Interestingly, the observations were compared to predictions based on a model of magnetic field angular dependence, and the system exhibited a complex interplay of different quantum states.

We've expanded the Sobocinay's Paterson and Zaki's propositional fragment of Pomset Logic to include the propositional fragment of Butler's BV, a more complex description logic, to encompass negative statements as well as product-like relationships between formulas. To determine the complexity of Pomset Logic, we've shown it to be equivalent to second-order logic with equality, while the more comprehensive BV logic surpasses it, displaying the properties of abstract data types. The complexity of BV logic was found to be higher, being more complex than Pomset Logic. The study also examined the fragment of Pomset Logic derived through the elimination of complex negative statements, revealing its equivalence to first-order logic with equality.

The pentagon identity for quantum dilogarithms and the five-term relation in Macdonald polynomials associated with operators discovered by Garsia and Mellit are both revealed as special cases within a broader "master pentagon identity" framework for the Ding-Iohara-Miki algebra. This general identity is confirmed through various checks, including a statistical one that utilizes the \(F_4\) root system.

We present photometric redshifts for a comprehensive dataset of 23,000 sources in the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields based on newly obtained deep infrared Ks-band observations, which were made as part of the 1.0-19.0 um Spitzer-IRAC W-CDF-S Legacy Program. By combining existing data from various telescopes with the UKIRT Wide-Field InfraRed Survey, we obtained 1.9 million measurements of the 23,000 sources in the 1.4 deg^2 area. We then used the LePhare spectral synthesis software to match these photometric data with various multi-band datasets, which were used to calculate the photometric redshifts using the probability-density-function method. The resulting photometric redshifts, which were determined using the Bayesian algorithm, demonstrate an accuracy of 25% for sources with i'-band magnitudes of 20.5 and 23.5, respectively. The obtained redshift catalog, which was cross-validated with existing redshift catalogs, is expected to be highly valuable for the scientific analysis of the Spitzer-IRAC W-CDF-S data.

Energy system planning's uncertainty issue is a long-standing concern that affects its success, yet traditional solution methods often ignore these uncertainties, focusing instead on simplifying models of a system. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a probabilistic decision support framework for addressing uncertainty in a comprehensive and practical approach. A case study comparing energy system scenarios is performed and the results indicate that the probabilistic method yields more accurate outcomes. Furthermore, this paper discusses the potential of probabilistic models to enhance decision-making across various policy applications.

We validate the statement presented in the title by establishing an explicit conversion framework between the two-electron wavefunction family and the matrix product state framework. Our examination of the two-electron Hilbert space reveals that only a limited subset of single-qubit and two-qubit operators are sufficient to construct all possible two-electron wavefunctions, which is achieved using a bond dimension of three matrix product state. Additionally, leveraging the matrix product state framework enables the construction of two-electron wavefunctions through a combination of two basic operations on single-qubit operators, which is equivalent to the classification of Young tableaux for two-party partitions.

A promising candidate for dark matter, vector sequence, is examined within a U(1)xU(1)xU(1) framework, where one $U(1)$ is unbroken. The complex triplet Higgs field responsible for a three-generation family of lepton masses also breaks two U(1) symmetries, yielding a non-Abelian dark matter particle and addressing lepton magnetic moment discrepancies.

Digital twins are crucial tools in tackling the pressing climate crisis that comes with the shift towards more extreme weather events. To this end, researchers are working to create a digital twin model that accurately predicts coastal flood levels and is based on complex numerical models. To this end, our study involves using neural operators to create a fast and accurate digital twin model. We've developed a novel approach that utilizes a hybrid physics-informed and physics-agnostic neural network to predict coastal flood levels. This approach combines the benefits of both perspectives and is applied to a well-established 2D shallow water model. Experimental results show that our approach significantly outperforms traditional physics-informed approaches, achieving even better results when combined with them. Moreover, our model is capable of handling real-world coastal flood risk assessments across multiple continents and can be improved further by fine-tuning its hyperparameters. The source code for our approach is openly available.

The open-source cosmology community has seen significant advancements in its ability to produce and disseminate research findings, with the BeyondPlanck and Cosmoglobe platforms leading this charge. By adopting an open-data approach, researchers can freely access and build upon previous research, fostering a culture of transparency and community collaboration. This approach not only ensures the long-term availability of scientific data but also enables researchers to build upon existing results, avoiding the need to collect and replicate data from proprietary sources. In this context, we reflect on our experiences with BeyondPlanck and Cosmoglobe, examine the benefits and challenges of open-data workflows, and explore potential avenues for further innovation and growth.

In reaction-diffusion systems, Turing patterns often emerge when a system reaches a critical threshold of instability. While Turing patterns are typically limited to smaller systems, they can be scaled up in networks where each node is connected to every other node, resulting in a vast, globally interconnected network. Building on previous research, which found that Turing patterns could form in such networks, even when the system is far beyond the instability threshold, our study shows that incorporating finite propagation constraints into the underlying network can significantly enhance the characteristics of the emerging patterns. We found that such propagation can lead to the emergence of more robust and persistent patterns, as well as to the appearance of new types of patterns that are dependent on the network topology.

The quantization of Yang-Mills theory has proven a difficult problem in the field of quantum field theory, with various approaches not yielding a clear and experimentally verified result. This problem's difficulty has led some to explore alternative theories, including quantum gravity models, where Yang-Mills theory is used to describe the interaction of particles. These particle interactions are often seen as the quantum geometry of spacetime, with the result that Yang-Mills theory is a crucial component of these models. This article will examine the problem of quantizing Yang-Mills theory within the framework of quantum gravity, with the result that the theory would be brought closer to a quasiclassical description. This description will be based on the use of a specific mathematical framework known as noncommutative differential geometry.

Our study focuses on wurtzite-based nanowires, which display remarkable optical and electronic properties due to their unique spatial confinement. We utilized a novel method involving scanning tunneling spectroscopy to investigate the surface properties of these nanowires, yielding unprecedented resolution at 0.03 eV per atom. The obtained results show that the surface electronic states of these nanowires exhibit direct transition characteristics, a finding that can be attributed to a uniform band alignment. The analysis also reveals that the surface electronic properties of these nanowires, including their band gap and the position of their conduction and valence bands, are aligned with their bulk counterparts. The presence of a unique, highly localized surface state within the band gap further supports the notion that the surface properties of these nanowires are similar to their bulk counterparts. The obtained results show that the surface properties of these nanowires are aligned with their bulk counterparts, indicating that the surface properties of these nanowires are not significantly affected by their bulk counterparts, even in cases of strong spatial confinement.

This paper outlines a data-driven approach to modeling negotiation strategies for an AI opponent in conversational dialogue. The proposed method leverages pre-existing data on human opponents' communication patterns to enhance opponent modeling. Specifically, it utilizes a simple transfer learning technique to adapt the communication model to a new opponent, leveraging unlabelled dialogue data and reducing the need for new data labels. The model's effectiveness is evaluated in the context of a sales conversation benchmark, showcasing its ability to apply insights from one opponent to another. Notably, preliminary results indicate that this approach outperforms a baseline model trained exclusively on data for the new opponent.

Kutasov and Cleaver's work introduced a novel method of compactifying segment like strings in string theory, offering an alternative to established Hilbert space quantization. This approach, however, requires the consideration of string tension, potentially derived from a dynamically generated one loop effective action resulting from the separation of D-branes. This action may be responsible for dynamically generating string tension, and our research explores the properties and dynamics of compactified like segment strings in both bosonic and superstring theories. We also investigate the effects of tachyon condensation on string tension, utilizing a suitable effective action. Furthermore, our study considers the possibility of cosmological models based on string like compactification and their implications for braneworld gravity.

Researchers have developed a method called the Online Design of Experiments (DOE) to tackle experimental inefficiencies stemming from insufficient sample size and inadequate data utilization. By integrating online matrix completion methods and optimization techniques, they've created innovative solutions that dynamically adjust experiment settings, such as adjusting factor levels or treatments, to minimize missing information. This approach, known as "balanced DOE," or "Balanced Experimental Design" (BED), effectively allocates observations to maximize the chances of filling in all remaining cells. However, the process of selecting an initial set of well-balanced experiments, called "designs," to facilitate this process remains unaddressed. By drawing inspiration from the concept of "pigeonhole principle," where at least one cell must be filled in any subset of a full design, researchers have formulated a problem to find the most informative or "optimal" subset. By solving this problem, they've created a framework that leverages existing DOE techniques to develop more efficient experimental designs, leading to significant reductions in the required number of experiments, such as 75% or more, without compromising any information.

The bond between covalent materials and ionic substrates appears unstable due to computational models indicating strong interfacial Coulomb interactions and lattice distortions. In contrast, molecular dynamics simulations have revealed a remarkably stable interface between Si and $\alpha$-Al$_2$O$_3$, which exhibits a low energy density and minimal ionic polarizations at the interface. Furthermore, the Si/Al$_2$O$_3$ interface exhibits robust dynamic stability, facilitating the transfer of energy between the materials. Notably, the Si/Al$_2$O$_3$ interface is thermodynamically stable, with a low formation energy that is substantiated by chemical potential arguments and confirmed by experimental data. A detailed analysis of the Si/Al$_2$O$_3$ interface has also identified the Si-Dangling Bond (SDB) as a key factor in its stability, which can be effectively passivated by hydrogen atoms to further enhance the interface's stability.

We investigated the collapse of spherically symmetric fields from general scalar field theories, translating the black hole formation process into a nonlinear dynamical system. Our approach yields well-posed systems, and we developed methods to numerically solve them. By employing nonlinear statistical models inspired by Gaussian processes, we demonstrated that these models effectively capture the underlying dynamics of field collapse, accurately predicting critical solutions associated with the anti-de Sitter spacetime. The models' performance in these simulations suggests they can be a valuable tool for modeling black hole collapse in theories with nonlinear scalar fields.

A comprehensive dataset spanning from 1966 to 2022 has been compiled to track container shipping industry metrics, covering a period marked by significant technological, economic, and political shifts. The dataset includes a 57-year record of second-hand and newbuilding ship prices divided into three segments, alongside freight rates and shipping quantity for a similar period. Notably, ship values have declined by two-fold since 1973, mirroring a pattern observed in oil prices at the time of the 1973 oil crisis. Subsequent decades saw a period of rapid growth, followed by a global economic downturn triggered by the global financial crisis in 2008.

The objective of online anomaly detection (OAD) is to identify, quantify, locate, and explain anomalies in real-time streams of data under the constraint of limited computational resources. OAD algorithms are typically evaluated on public datasets using a variety of metrics, but there remains a scarcity of comprehensive comparisons. Our investigation aims to bridge this gap by conducting a meta-analysis of various OAD methods, focusing on their performance, efficiency, and hyperparameter settings on six distinct datasets. Our findings, which are presented in two stages, reveal that different OAD methods excel on different datasets and suggest that algorithm choice should depend on the specific application. Moreover, our study demonstrates that even the most advanced OAD methods can achieve superior performance when their hyperparameters are optimally set, but this can significantly increase computational costs.

The most widespread and aggressive form of brain tumors is glioma, often necessitating precise tumor volume measurement for optimal treatment planning. However, manual segmentation can be extremely time-consuming and often yields inconsistent results. This study introduces an automated method for the precise segmentation of gliomas in multi-modal MRI datasets, utilizing convolutional neural networks combined with a low-complexity post-processing approach. Our network was trained on a dataset of 84 gliomas and demonstrated exceptional accuracy when evaluating a separate, unseen dataset of 20 cases. In particular, the J-Score and Dice coefficient metrics revealed a remarkably high agreement between predicted and actual tumor boundaries, while the Hausdorff distance metric showed a relatively low discrepancy of 2.4 mm. Given the complexity of brain tumors, particularly in low-contrast areas, our method's reliability is promising for future clinical applications, potentially saving time and reducing inter-observer discrepancies in manual assessments.

A type of low-energy spin excitation, known as a triplon, is a result of spin wave splitting in magnetic materials. The triplon exhibits characteristics of both bosons and Higgs particles, with real-world implications in materials science and quantum physics. To investigate its role in magnetic material transport, we've conducted experiments involving the warm-up of a well-studied antiferromagnetic material, with subsequent triplon emission influencing its electrical conductivity. The observed current reduction is found to be linked to the triplon's energy, with a specific measurement matching theoretical predictions for this particular material. The triplon's role in reducing transport energy further supports its potential role in carrying heat across solids.

This article introduces the concept of statistical convergence via asymptotic density via a free net in a topological space, drawing inspiration from the work of Bagirov and Ramanujan, while expanding upon the work of Šujovs, proposing the concept of statistical convergence of asymptotic points generated by a directed set in a topological abelian group, and establishing a link between the convergence of free nets and the convergence of a subsequence of image net.

This study employs discontinuous Galerkin finite element methods to solve the one-dimensional Rosenau equation and presents a comprehensive analysis, encompassing consistency checks, error bound analyses, error bound examinations, and numerical simulations to verify the results.

We investigate a coupled linear model of compressible and incompressible fluids, and we establish well-posedness in the linearized case under the assumption that the incompressible fluid has infinite boundary viscosity. By leveraging an inf-sup condition, we demonstrate that the associated stationary and evolution problems satisfy a unique saddle-point structure, and in turn, a semigroup well-posedness theory can be developed for this system. Furthermore, we present a wave interaction potential that underlies the semigroup well-posedness result and, through this connection, we verify well-posedness for a related nonlinear version in the context of small-amplitude perturbations.

The interaction between two particles that share a common quantum state can give rise to a complex state of matter known as a bi-particle condensate. This type of state has been observed in two dimensions and in two particles, but a similar occurrence in three dimensions and with more particles remains a mystery. A new state of matter has been proposed, consisting of charged particles arranged in a crystalline structure triggered by an external magnetic field. This proposed state can be achieved in materials known as van der Waals heterostructures, which are composed of layers with weak interlayer interactions. The suggested state generalizes the concept of a Bose-Einstein condensate to charged pairs. The proposed state also exhibits a non-zero spin density, a feature that has been predicted to occur in excitons at the interface of two materials. The predicted state can be observed in two different configurations, one in which the spin density is concentrated at the interface and another in which the spin density is evenly distributed across the material.

The LAMOST telescope has been used to collect a vast amount of data from stellar spectra, containing valuable information on over 3 million candidate exoplanet stars. To make the most of this data, it's essential to calibrate the radial velocity of these stars with high precision. To achieve this, researchers have developed a calibration method based on multiple reference star observations. They have created a calibration catalog containing RV values of high precision for 1,253 fast-moving stars, sourced from data cross-checked by multiple sources. When applied to 1,972 fast-moving LAMOST spectra, the resulting radial velocity errors were found to be around 1.1 km/s. To further improve accuracy, researchers have developed an enhanced calibration model that utilizes a complex mathematical function to account for specific spectral patterns in stars with multiple spectral peaks. When applied to 1,984 LAMOST spectra, the enhanced model yielded radial velocity errors of 0.5 km/s or less. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new calibration method and the enhanced model, and they have been incorporated into a new calibration catalog.

We propose a novel approach to solve the inverse scattering problem using a deep learning framework that exploits certain symmetries present in the problem. By employing two types of neural networks - equivariant networks for feature propagation and CNNs for feature aggregation, we successfully derive a comprehensive solution to the wide-band inverse scattering problem. Our approach allows for the training of the solution using randomly generated scattering data, eliminating the need for a forward solver. By demonstrating the efficacy of our method through numerical experiments, we have achieved results that approach the accuracy of existing algorithms but with a significantly reduced computational cost.

Reliability engineering utilizes accelerated degradation testing (ADT) to assess the lifespan of complex systems with multiple components. This method determines the distribution of the system's performance metrics under various stress conditions. This research focuses on improving the estimation of mixed distribution tails by applying bivariate gamma models to ADT, considering the relationship between two system components. It suggests using the copula function to model the connection between these components and proposes a non-parametric test to assess the significance of including the copula in the model. This method also introduces a new statistical approach to accurately estimate the upper tail of a mixed distribution by using data from two measurement points, as well as an asymptotic theory for the estimate's convergence rate.

We utilize the multiphase transport model (AMPT) to investigate the triangular flow $v_3$ in 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions at high energies. The research indicates that the observed $v_3$ values are primarily driven by the initial anisotropic triangular flow of participant nucleons, rather than any differences in hadronization or flow evolution. Furthermore, the model's predictions for $v_3$ align with experimental measurements.

The interaction between solar wind high-speed streams and interplanetary coronal mass ejections has been linked to various geomagnetic storm intensifiers known as interplanetary coronal mass ejection-driven substorms.  To better understand how ICMEs influence HSSs, we analyzed data from the Magnetometer and Plasma Instrumentation (MAG) and Plasma Instrumentation Field Line Experiment (PIFE) instruments on board Parker Solar Probe.  Our study, which is the first to use plasma parameters such as beta, plasma beta squared, and plasma beta squared subtracted from magnetic field, offers new insights into ICME characteristics.  By utilizing a novel approach, we identified ICMEs within PSP's observations and investigated their impact on HSSs, which we also classified based on plasma properties.  Our findings reveal that the plasma characteristics of these ICMEs, which we call "ICME-A," differ from those of typical ICMEs, leading to increased plasma and beta values.  Furthermore, we observed a significant impact of these ICME-A events on HSSs, which we classified based on plasma properties.  Our study provides evidence of a unique relationship between ICMEs and HSSs, which we believe will be a valuable resource for future studies examining the effects of ICMEs on Earth's magnetic field.

The simulation of mobile ad hoc networks relies heavily on the random waypoint mobility model due to its frequent use. However, existing algorithms for simulating this model are limited by their inability to accurately represent the long-term stability of the network, as they often neglect the effects of a node remaining stationary for an extended period. Furthermore, mobility models that account for this characteristic are often computationally expensive and impractical for large-scale network simulations. In an effort to resolve this issue, we have developed a novel stochastic approach called the exponential time-to-stationary model, which enables the simulation of mobile ad hoc networks with more accurate representations of node movement.

The $\phi$ decaying into $K^+K^-$ particles was studied utilizing the BaBar experiment's large dataset. These data were compared to predictions made by chiral perturbation theory, particularly in the region where $m(K^+K^- - K^+K^-$) approaches $2m_K$. A comprehensive examination of the $K^+K^-$ system was performed, yielding the first experimental determination of the $A_0$ parameter associated with the $K^+K^-$ to $2K^+K^-$ transition amplitude. This parameter was found to be $A_0 = 0.0024 \pm 0.0001 \mathrm{(stat.)} \pm 0.0001 \mathrm{(syst.).}$ The analysis included an investigation of the $K^+K^-$ mass distribution near the $2m_K$ threshold, which revealed a small, detectable peak. This peak's significance was found to be $2.9 \sigma$ for the left-hand side of the $K^+K^-$ system and $1.5 \sigma$ for the right-hand side.

The microscopic inertial masses related to isovector currents in nuclear systems are calculated using the non-ground state local random phase approximation, with the isoscalar and isovector effective nucleon interactions. The computed inertial masses are compared to those derived from empirical values of monopole and dipole transition energies, with the results showing a strong correlation. The results also reveal a direct connection between inertial masses and nucleon effective masses. Utilizing these calculated values, the cross-sections for symmetric and asymmetric fission processes, as well as nuclear reactions involving proton and neutron elastic scattering, are estimated.

The field of Abstraction and Reasoning (AR) is rapidly expanding, with a notable increase in publications and initiatives such as the establishment of the NeurIPS Abstraction and Reasoning Foundation. This new foundation has initiated the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, a comprehensive dataset of 120,000 images categorized into three distinct categories: graphs featuring dual-colored nodes or edges, images containing text, and images featuring a dominant color. This article provides an in-depth analysis of the three classes and identifies the most effective search strategies for each.

This paper explores the common Riemann problem for nonlinear conservation laws with jumps in flux, influenced by discontinuities in their coefficients and their interactions with boundaries. We are particularly interested in the fractional solutions that emerge from the interaction between an inviscid and viscous approximation. By examining the limit of vanishing viscosity under certain conditions, we identify a solution within the fractional regularity class for problems with specific flux functions, including the Burgers equation. This solution, restricted to the parabolic regularity class, is obtained through a different inviscid limit procedure.

Measurements of the $B_{s}^{2}$ decay rates into $D_{s}^{\mp} K^{\pm}$ and $D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ final states have been conducted using 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ of pp collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at 7 and 8 TeV centre-of-mass energies. The $B_{s}^{2}$ decay rates have been found to be 0.5950 $\pm$ 0.0016 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.0104 (syst.) $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ for $D_{s}^{+}$ and 0.5683 $\pm$ 0.0018 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.0087 (syst.) $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ for $D_{s}^{-}$. The $B^{0}$ decay rate to $D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ was found to be 0.03704 $\pm$ 0.00039 (stat.) $\pm$ 0.00057 (syst.) $\times$ 10$^{-3}$. These results are in line with other studies and with the Standard Model predictions.

This letter's focus is on the uplink spectral efficiency of cell-free massive MIMO systems employing multicarrier division duplex mode, particularly when utilizing narrow band or hybrid massive MIMO approaches. By utilizing a Gaussian approximation of local field, we establish an uplink MIMO channel's lower bound on the large scale, which is found to be equivalent to a linear combination of its downlink counterparts. Subsequently, we derive the maximum uplink spectral efficiency of cell-free systems, demonstrating that their performance is comparable to that of downlink, with additional benefits resulting from increased spatial and frequency resources.

The shuffle model of differential privacy recently gained attention due to its potential to achieve high utility while maintaining privacy. Although the utility of the shuffle model has been extensively studied, the tight lower bounds on its privacy costs remain unknown. In this study, we fill this knowledge gap by analyzing the $\epsilon$-DP shuffle model with a focus on both non-uniform and uniform random shuffling. Specifically, we establish tight lower bounds on the accuracy of $k$-dimensional histograms under $\epsilon$-DP and demonstrate that the accuracy of $k$-dimensional histograms under the $\epsilon$-DP idle server shuffle model is $\Omega\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon^2}{k^2}}}\right)$. Furthermore, we establish tight lower bounds on the accuracy of $k$-dimensional histograms under the $\epsilon$-DP lazy server shuffle model, which is a more practical model in comparison to the idle server model. In addition to lower bounds, we also establish upper bounds on the accuracy of $k$-dimensional histograms under the $\epsilon$-DP idle server shuffle model and the $\epsilon$-DP lazy server shuffle model, and we also extend the results to the more practical local ($\epsilon$-DP-l) server shuffle model.

This research introduces a new orthogonal multiplexing technique known as Orthogonal Time Sequency Multiplexing Modulation, which improves upon the conventional approach by utilizing a unique symbol structure. In OTSM, each frame is divided into multiple segments, with each segment carrying information based on the amplitude and phase of its constituent samples. A key innovation in OTSM is its utilization of a new sampling basis, which ensures that information across segments is orthogonal to one another. As a result, receiver processing can be simplified significantly. A comprehensive analysis of OTSM's performance under various conditions such as additive white Gaussian noise and fading channels is provided. A straightforward receiver architecture is proposed, with a significant reduction in computational complexity compared to OTSM's original implementation. Our analysis demonstrates that the new receiver exhibits improved error rate performance while maintaining a high degree of simplicity.

Let's denote the weight on a semigroup $S$ as $\omega$. The $\ell^1$ algebra with weighted norm $\| \cdot\|_{\omega}$ has the operator norm less than or equal to $\max\{2, \omega\}$ times the weighted norm $\| \cdot\|_\omega$. If the weight $\omega$ is monotonically increasing and has a finite value $\| \omega\|_{\infty}$, then the weighted $\ell^1$ algebra has the operator norm less than or equal to $2\| \omega\|_{\infty}$. This bound is also achievable.

Molten metal melt pools are studied using a computational model that simulates the behavior of solidification and melting using a two-dimensional, axisymmetric approach. The model is coupled with thermal transfer and solves for melt pool dynamics in a conduction mode, using a laser spot with variable size and position. Numerical results are validated against experimental data from a conduction-mode laser melting process, revealing the formation of complex melt pool structures. The research investigates how variations in melt pool shape impact free surface curvature, identifying key characteristics such as the formation of double humps and jet formation.

This research proposes an innovative architecture for supporting the energy needs of moving public transport buses, leveraging the key technologies of intelligent reflecting surfaces, wireless energy transfer, and mobile edge computing. The energy requirements of onboard vehicles are met through wireless energy reception from base station transceivers. These transceutors simultaneously process data from mobile edge computing servers. The technology of intelligent reflecting surfaces adjusts the energy and data signals received by moving buses, ensuring optimal transmission efficiency. To optimize system performance, a novel optimization framework is developed, combining the energy transfer, data processing, and signal reflection functions. The framework is formulated as a complex optimization problem that is efficiently solved using a method called alternating optimization, which uses a form of iterative optimization. The results from simulations demonstrate that this system effectively meets the energy needs of moving buses, processes data at a high speed, and efficiently uses the signal components. The results also show that this technology significantly enhances the energy transfer efficiency of moving buses.

The measure of approximate degree of a Boolean function, which is the lowest degree $d$ of a real-valued polynomial that approximates the function, has been found to have a connection with several other similar measures of complexity. The measure of approximate degree, in particular, is the lowest among several other measures of complexity, including polynomial degree, in terms of several other models of complexity. Researchers have previously demonstrated that for certain types of Boolean functions, the measure of approximate degree is equivalent to other measures of complexity known as $\epsilon$-approximating degree and $\epsilon$-Nisan-Wigdorff degree. In this study, we prove that for a particular type of Boolean functions, the measure of approximate degree is equivalent to another measure of complexity known as the CNF-Degree. This result is significant because it extends a previous finding of similar equivalence to another type of Boolean functions known as DNF. By combining this result with an existing upper bound of approximate degree, we were able to establish a lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ on the approximate degree of CNF formulas. This finding is the first lower bound of this magnitude that was known for this type of Boolean function. In addition, we were able to establish several other upper and lower bounds of approximate degree for several other types of Boolean functions, including CNF formulas, DNF formulas, and decision lists. The findings of this study also have implications for several other models of complexity, including polynomial degree, $\epsilon

This paper employs the Conley index to prove the presence of periodic solutions with specific stability characteristics within a class of autonomous differential equations. Such solutions feature distinct physical properties, including a sudden, sudden change from one to another attractor, resulting in abrupt transitions between different patterns. The derived results are then applied to examine bistability in three biological systems, namely, a predator-prey model, a generalized Scott-Rotenberg reaction-diffusion equation, and a simplified Neumann model representing a membrane vessel.

This research investigates the thermal and magnetic field properties of quark matter within strange quark stars using a modified Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model, considering finite temperature and magnetic field conditions. We examine the stable and unstable regions of quark matter in relation to phase transitions and conduct a thermal analysis of quark matter density profiles. Furthermore, we investigate how the magnetic field affects the rotational properties of strange quark stars, including their mass, radius, surface temperature, and redshift factor.

In recent years, research on audiovisual correspondence or bi-modal learning has gained significant momentum, driven by potential applications in multimedia, entertainment, and human-computer interaction. A primary challenge in current deep learning models is the lack of labeled, controlled audio-visual data, necessitating the use of unsupervised learning techniques. However, existing methods often struggle with audio-visual synchronization errors, inaccurate predictions, and limited generalizability. 

This article offers a comprehensive overview of the recent advancements in deep audio-visual correlation learning, including novel unsupervised learning methods, entropic loss functions, and entropic correlation measures. We also discuss joint learning of audio-visual models, self-supervised audio-visual alignment, and audio-visual datasets creation. We provide insights into current successes and future research directions in audio-visual correlation learning.

The Linear Ordering Problem (LOP) is a fundamental model in combinatorial optimization, dealing with the process of assigning labels to n distinct entities based on specific preference constraints. LOP's applications span multiple fields, including data visualization, network analysis, and machine learning. LOP's generalization, the Weighted Linear Ordering Problem (WLOP), incorporates weights to represent varying levels of importance. LOP and WLOP are highly challenging combinatorial optimization problems, with NP-hard complexity and difficult approximation, with no known polynomial-time approximation factor higher than 1.39. LOP's solution reliability, or non-applicability, in certain real-world scenarios, is a critical concern. This paper introduces a probabilistic approach to LOP and WLOP, with the goal of measuring solution reliability and developing algorithms for small-weight instances. A new method for estimating solution reliability is presented, along with an improved lower bound for WLOP and a new parameterized algorithm with a two-sided randomized running time of $\mathcal{O}^{*}(2^{(4n-m-\ell)\log d}\cdot (n+m)\log n)$, where $n$ represents the number of entities, $m$ denotes the number of constraints, and $\ell$ is the number of large weights.

Superconducting thin films of NbN were produced on substrates made of sapphire and Si(1 0), utilizing a DC-magnetron source that relied on PentaGraphite as a supplemental target. Thin films were analyzed for their superconducting properties at temperatures between 1.7 K and 40 K and frequencies between 10 MHz and 80 MHz. Conductance measurements were conducted using a complex measurement method, resulting in two-dimensional diagrams that showed the superconducting characteristics of these thin films. Data indicated that superconductivity in these thin films is characterized by two distinct phenomena - a transition from a single superconducting state to a state with multiple superconducting phases, and another transition from a state with multiple superconducting phases to a state without superconducting phases. These transitions are observed in two different temperature ranges, and they both correlate with an increase in superconducting state fluctuations. It was also found that these thin films have a high critical temperature, and they can be driven into a state with high resistivity by applying a certain magnetic field.

In this paper, we present Temporal Regular Path Queries (TRPQ), a novel class of temporal queries capable of expressing intricate temporal patterns across diverse relational databases. These queries incorporate time constraints in three ways: the timestamp of relationships, the age of data values, and the temporal intervals defining the objects. We show that TRPQ can be efficiently evaluated within logarithmic space and polynomial time by developing a model that decouples the temporal constraints from the underlying logic program, thereby facilitating a pre-computation approach. We further enhance the TRPQ framework with Temporal Aggregation Path Queries (TRPQ+), which enables the integration of aggregation functions like sum and average. Notably, our approach can be adapted to incorporate constraints based on temporal intervals.

The development of precise optical techniques for cooling molecules has led to the creation of highly stable and cold molecular clocks with exceptional accuracy, as well as the facilitation of novel experiments in chemistry and physics. To achieve this technological advancement, researchers have been working to develop efficient methods for optical cooling of molecules. Free radicals, which are highly reactive, serve as ideal subjects to simulate chemical reactions and explore molecular interactions. Despite their reactivity, these molecules have not been successfully cooled using standard methods due to their highly unstable nature. This paper presents a new approach to the cooling of free radicals by utilizing the interaction between lithium atoms and free radicals in a deceleration experiment. The results show that the velocity distribution of free radicals can be significantly reduced by over two orders of magnitude. The velocity reduction is attributed to the strong van der Waals interaction between lithium atoms and free radicals, allowing for the formation of long-lived complexes that facilitate velocity selection. The maximum achievable velocity selectivity scales linearly with the number of free radical bonds, with a maximum of 1000-fold for three bond-free radicals. The velocity reduction is limited by the lithium beam density and the presence of triatomic products. The maximum achieved mean velocity of 150 m/s represents a significant milestone in the cooling of polyatomic free radicals.

We introduce a catalogue called Living Swift-XRT Point Source that offers real-time
location and classification details for transient events within a 10 arcminute radius
around Swift's primary pointing direction. It provides information on transient
probability, XRT pointing, cross-references with other databases like ZTF and ATel,
and links to AMPEL's transient detection pages. Our catalogue utilizes the
AMPEL transient detection software in real-time to identify transient events within
the specified radius by monitoring XRT data and cross-referencing with other
databases. We estimate that our system can detect 80% of point-like X-ray transients
within a 5-second timescale and 50% within a 1-second timescale, making it highly
sensitive to short-lived transient events. With a 5-second timescale and a 1-second
timescale detection efficiency of 84.6% and 53.4%, respectively, our catalogue
provides valuable information for researchers. We also describe the catalogue's
parameters and offer examples of its applications in transient studies.

We examine the ground state of the spin-1/2 J1-J2 XY model on a square lattice and its connection to the plaquette valence-bond state. Employing a strong quantum Monte Carlo method, we calculated the exact ground state for various lattice sizes and on a large number of quantum Monte Carlo trajectories. We discovered that in the XY model, the plaquette valence-bond state is the ground state and the order parameter is inversely proportional to the square of the lattice size. We also found that in the XY model, the correlation length is significantly larger than in the J1-J2 Heisenberg model, and the large-scale bond pattern is consistent with the proposed bond pattern of the plaquette valence-bond state. We conclude that the ground state of the XY model is more suitable for a new state of matter characterized by large correlation length and the PVB state.

This study employs a three-dimensional panel data model to the international trade decomposition technique initially proposed by Kakanda & Kiy & Matsumoto (2021). This method dissects net bilateral trade dynamics into net imports and net exports using a two-dimensional panel data model. Our approach expands this method to a time frame of trade agreements by incorporating a time dimension. We validate the efficiency of the proposed method through simulations. Furthermore, the method is applied to examine Japan's bilateral trade relationships within the ASEAN region from 1970 to 2018.

We introduce a noncommutative deformation of four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory, utilizing the $L_{\infty}$ bootstrap method to analyze solutions of the deformed $L_{\infty}$ homotopy algebra. The deformation leads to the emergence of noncommutative two-forms, enabling the deformation of classical gauge potentials into noncommutative gauge potentials. The presence of noncommutative two-forms gives rise to a noncommutative two-form gauge field, a novel concept in four-dimensional spacetime. We further extend this work to the study of non-Abelian gauge theories, revealing that the gauge couplings are dependent on the spacetime coordinates and transforming under the gauge group.

The application of classical equalization techniques to optical quantum systems is explored. Building on established principles for optical quantum systems and utilizing coherent superposition, a unique coherent equalizer is developed in this study. The proposed approach is applicable to both lossy and lossless channels and utilizes complete-state measurement for equalization. A key benefit of this method is its adaptability, enabling it, for instance, to effectively utilize spatial-mode entanglement for quantum key distribution. Additionally, this study demonstrates the feasibility of re-purposing coherent equalizers for classical applications by introducing a classical noise channel into a quantum setup, thereby creating a lossless quantum channel, and subsequently enhancing classical channel transmission quality.

Individuals experiencing mental health disorders often struggle to accurately perceive time, a symptom commonly observed in conditions such as schizophrenia, major depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Current methods for tracking this symptom reliance on questionnaires, which can be infrequent and prone to inaccuracy. This research introduces a new framework to monitor time perception by leveraging wearable technology, utilizing a smartwatch to collect data on individuals' gait and movement patterns. Our study, which combined data from wearable wristbands and smartphones, demonstrated the effectiveness of this approach in predicting when an individual perceives a time interval as taking more than 5 minutes. This ability to forecast this behavior is crucial in monitoring the progression of mental health conditions and assessing treatment efficacy.

This research investigates the relationship between decision-making speed and quality, utilizing a unique data set from tax inspectors in India. The findings reveal that quicker evaluations are generally associated with lower quality assessments. The study suggests that individuals with greater experience tend to produce higher quality outputs early in their careers, with quality then declining as experience is not a limiting factor. The data also indicate that individuals prefer slower evaluations due to personal and psychological costs involved. The implications of these findings align with the literature suggesting that simpler tasks may yield greater efficiency gains.

Previous research has identified significant ideological discrepancies in machine learning fairness definitions, which differ in their underlying assumptions and the legal concepts they represent. While some definitions are based on the law of intentional discrimination, others draw upon the concept of liability in tort law. This disparity can be reflected in how different models are evaluated, depending on the legal framework used. Our research provides a formal explanation of these similarities and contradictions using tort law principles to clarify the implications of various fairness metrics. Furthermore, our work highlights potential issues with existing definitions under specific legal standards, which can be resolved by incorporating concepts from tort law for fairness evaluation.

A novel method of producing high-intensity soft X-ray fluorescence using a band gap excitation in trivalent lanthanoid ions has been discovered. By employing this technique in a specific crystal, a novel process for generating polarized X-rays through the emission of pairs of Majorana/Dirac neutrinos is made possible. The unique properties of the X-rays produced can be precisely controlled by adjusting the parameters of the ion, thus providing a potential means of detecting the Dirac nature of neutrinos and potentially even their handedness.

We have investigated both single- and double-strangeness hypernuclei, with atomic numbers from 2 to 5 and protonic charges from 1 to 5, in the context of strangeness-strangeness interaction. By employing the $\chi\)PT calculations up to order $Q^4$, our results for $\Lambda$ hyperon binding energies in the 1S0 state align with empirical data, while in the 3P1 state, our findings show significant discrepancies. Furthermore, our analysis suggests that applying a universal strangeness-strangeness interaction to calculate double-strangeness hypernuclei in the 1S0 state is not only feasible but also yields results comparable to those of $^{6}_{\Lambda\Sigma}^{17}$Cl.

Social media platforms such as Facebook and Instagram have become essential tools for users. However, these platforms pose significant risks to users' privacy, including the potential misuse of personal data collected online. To address these concerns, we developed MetaPriv, a novel Android app that prioritizes user privacy. MetaPriv is designed to work in conjunction with popular social media platforms, automatically detecting and preventing malicious activities driven by advertising or profit motives. By employing a rule-based system, MetaPriv enables users to customize their privacy settings, including the option to block sensitive data sharing and third-party extensions. To enhance the platform's capabilities, we propose the creation of a community-driven repository to store and share privacy rules, ensuring that users receive a comprehensive security solution. Our research demonstrates the effectiveness of MetaPriv in safeguarding user privacy, with the app currently available for download at 1.0.0-beta.

Consider a classic Bienaym\'e-Galton-Watson process and associate with it a coalescent graph, which can be viewed as a discrete-time process of a sequence of apheres. In this discrete-time process, a new individual enters the apheres at time n; the new individual branches off into as many new individuals as there are existing individuals in the apheres, with each branch having a random number of offspring according to a Poisson distribution. This Poisson distribution is conditioned on the number of existing individuals in the apheres. This process is a classic representation of a multi-type Galton-Watson process with a varying environment, which has been extensively studied by. El'sertee El showed that the process can be represented by a point process, which has a renewal structure. This paper aims to further analyze the process by characterizing the process's waiting times between apheres, which are termed "gaps".
